business: MOV, a social all-sport fitness & nutrition app with CSV import, multi-sport tracking, Strava-style social network, RPG stat progression, and tiered AI coaching
target: Active adults, 18 to 40, who lift weights and play recreational sports (padel, tennis, soccer, swimming, running), track nutrition, and want a social community and RPG progression for their fitness
where: Online, iOS App Store, Google Play Store, Worldwide

behaviours.name: Multi-sport recreational athlete
behaviours.how: Lifts 2-3x a week, plays padel, soccer, or tennis on weekends, swims or runs, tired of tracking across 3 apps.

behaviours.name: Strava & social fitness lover
behaviours.how: Active on Strava, loves kudos, leaderboards, and sharing athletic accomplishments with friends.

behaviours.name: Uses Strong/Hevy/MyFitnessPal
behaviours.how: Has years of lifting data in Strong or Hevy, hesitant to switch unless 1-click CSV import works flawlessly.

behaviours.name: Gamer / RPG progression fan
behaviours.how: Motivated by leveling up stats (Agility, Strength, Endurance), unlocking titles, and seeing visual character progress.

behaviours.name: Referral & freemium optimizer
behaviours.how: Loves free tiers, eager to invite 5 friends to unlock free Pro months.

behaviours.name: Data & analytics nerd
behaviours.how: Obsessed with calorie burn accuracy, MET calculations, bodyweight metrics, and macro tracking.

objections: Are my friends already on MOV or will the social feed feel empty at the beginning?
Will 1-click CSV import actually preserve all my past PRs and history from Strong or Hevy without breaking?
How accurate is the calorie burn calculation for sports like padel, tennis, and swimming based on my weight/height?
Is 5 AI meal scans a week enough on the free tier, and is Pro ($4.99/mo or $29.99/yr) worth it if I can invite 5 friends for free Pro?
Does the app feel bloated trying to do lifting, sports, social, and food all in one, or is the UI clean and fast?
habits: you play padel, soccer, or tennis on weekends and lift weights during the week
you check friends' workouts on social feeds and love friendly competition
you log sets on your phone between gym exercises and hate slow, cluttered interfaces
you enjoy seeing your stats level up like an RPG character (e.g. boosting Agility from soccer)
you love sharing referral links if the reward is a free month of Pro
